chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Idris ibn al-Hasan, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, walnuts and cheese, when they are combined, are a cure, and when they are separated, they are an illness.
ai.seo_question: What is the health benefit of combining walnuts and cheese according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reflects the Shia tradition of integrating practical medicine with spiritual wisdom, emphasizing the concept of *tadafu'* (mutual interaction) in food properties. It underscores the scholarly view that the health benefits of food are not merely intrinsic but depend on their combination, a principle often cited in classical Islamic medical texts like those of Ibn Sina. This teaching serves as both a dietary guideline and a metaphor for how disparate elements can either heal or harm depending on their unity or separation.
